body: Review-scope approval: dotfiles-T88-parallel-execution-rule-a01 at PR #243 head 62845ab9 (substantive commits e50150df, e68eb6a7, c544c79f, 8978517d, c5706e2e, d609c768, 0aed931c, 0407fb07, d0f03418, 99f84926, 0189cfb3, fb4c9a9a, 62845ab9; update-branch merges through main f2b5c115; 3 files). Orchestrator read every hunk at c8d31501 and the SKILL-only revise diff to 04fd9425: the rule gains the parallel-execution invariant (pairwise-disjoint code files, prose in disjoint sections, three workers counting the pair worker, dispatch bounded to free seats, re-task at once, acceptance in RESULT order, audits queued on the single tab), the seat-capability routing invariant and the T64-aligned nested-worktree bullet; the SKILL adds the parallel procedure (now: next task on a fresh branch from origin/main with the previous branch kept until acceptance; `gh pr update-branch` for every in-flight PR whose base moved, prose or code), routing by allowed files including permgate edits to a Codex security-profile worker (cited to the model-selection rule), the classifier-denial boundary, and step 14 rewritten after a scratch verification on crit v0.21.1: a Claude Plan Mode worker reports `plan-mode-used=<worktree>` and does nothing else, because `crit stop` misses a server started on another branch, `crit stop <plan-file>` never matches a plan session, and a sandboxed pgrep sees only the sandbox pid namespace; the orchestrator lists `pgrep -fl _serve`, confirms the cwd from ~/.crit/sessions/*.json and kills the worker's server as host hygiene. Audit of e50150df: four findings (two fixed in e68eb6a7, audited correct; two step-14 findings fixed in c544c79f/c5706e2e). Seven Codex threads fixed in-PR, all replied and resolved; thumbs-up on 04fd9425 at 04:02:29Z, CI green, mergeable CLEAN. Round 2 (task-level audit of 04fd9425): step 14 covers any worker whose session started a Crit plan review (a Codex seat does so through the Crit plugin Stop hook `crit plan-hook --mode codex`), the orchestrator confirms a server is live (`ps -o args=`) before `kill` and removes stale records, and the sandbox artifact records the scratch server. Decision 4 and the P1 that followed: a seat never edits the source of its own execution boundary, so every emitter of a Claude seat's boundary (claude.permissions, claude.sandbox, claude.hooks, codex writable roots rendered into allowWrite, the renderer, the rendered settings, the merge script) is routed to a Codex worker or the operator; the orchestrator runs host cleanup outside its sandbox via the permission gate; the worker kind stays the manifest's (not-applicable). Eleven Codex threads in total, ten fixed in-PR and one not-applicable, all replied and resolved. Rounds 3-5 (task-level audits of 19becfc5, 5bef5588, 0189cfb3): the orchestrator verifies the live process cwd before killing a Crit server; the rule bullet routes permgate like the SKILL; the worker commits and pushes before RESULT and takes a clean checkpoint before every branch switch, so a revise re-checks out the earlier branch safely; routing follows the boundary a change touches (Claude-only to a Codex seat, Codex-only to a Claude seat, both or unsplittable to the operator, kind recorded in the task file). Fourteen Codex threads: twelve fixed in-PR, two not-applicable (manifest worker kind; rule prose is not the execution boundary). Round 6: permgate is both seats' hook, so edits to it go to the operator and the Codex security-profile worker reviews the change before acceptance (the model-selection rule assigns that worker to security audits, not to editing permgate); the paginated final-head Bot poll is pasted. Rule words 1269 → about 1500, for T83 to shrink.
